Triage: lands in the retirement **method** — `.claude/skills/spec-property-retirement` and the evidence step it prescribes ⇒ **`domain:skills`**. Route only — ⛔ not graded here (that lane self-triages its own findings).

## ⚠️ Routed with an explicit note that this is not an ordinary route-only card

⭐ **I have first-hand corroboration of instance 1, from four hours ago.** This seat closed **#15180** `not_planned` at R+173 after independently re-measuring `resolveViewDescription` (`i18n-resolver.ts:424` → `:908` → the dispatch table → `packages/rest`, lit control `resolveViewLabel` = 5). The key is read server-side and reaches the served document. ⇒ **The card's account of instance 1 is exactly right**, verified by a different seat by a different route.

⚠️ And instance 2 is the worse one: **#15184 had already reached a maintainer ruling** (A — retire) before its premise was measured false. ⇒ A method that produces false "dead" verdicts does not merely waste a round; it can carry a **maintainer's signature** onto the deletion of a working channel.

⇒ ⛔ Both rounds shipped nothing only because their dispatch orders carried an explicit stop condition. That is the control that held — and it is a control on the **dispatch**, not on the method. The method itself is unguarded.

## ⭐ Why this belongs to the skills lane and not to spec

The card's own framing is 「a defect in **how "dead key" is being established**」, ⛔ not in any one key. The evidence step it indicts is prescribed by the retirement playbook — a **governed surface** — so the fix lands there and on the governed path (human terminal), whatever the census tool does. ⚠️ If the skills seat reads the fix as landing in `packages/spec/liveness/**` instead, that re-routes to `domain:spec`; ⛔ I am not pre-empting that call.

## For the grading seat, ⛔ not a grade

⭐ The two faults worth carrying into any fix: **"zero authored instances in our own repos" is not evidence of deadness** (the decisive control is one command, and the card names it), and **cross-repo liveness evidence rots faster than the verdict it supports**. ⇒ The second is the structural one: a verdict outlives the reading that justified it, and nothing expires it.

⚠️ Related, ⛔ not duplicate: **#17546** (filed by this seat at R+173) is the *documentation* half of instance 1 — stale prose naming retired symbols, which is what misled #15180. This card is the **method**; #17546 is one thing the method mis-read.

Two retirements in one day rested on those gaps (#15180 closed `not_planned` on re-measurement by the triage seat; #15184 reached a maintainer ruling on a false premise), stopped only by the dispatch orders' stop conditions — a guard on the dispatch, not on the method. `finding` dropped; **`pm:queue` · `Task` · `priority:p2`**. Direction (seat reading, veto window in the round report): the playbook's evidence step gains the three bindings as rules, paid by density inside the file — (1) a census offered as 「dead」 evidence runs with a known-live sibling key as its control and reports both readings (a control that scores the same as the subject has measured nothing); (2) a `cross-repo` liveness row cited as an argument is re-verified at citation time — the path exists, the lines resolve — because the row's `verifiedAt` clock is not the citing seat's; (3) 「zero authored instances」 ≠ 「no code reads it」 — a retirement needs the second. ⛔ Not: `packages/spec/liveness/**` or `elsewhere.mts` (the spec lane — the triage seat's re-route condition; the seat reads the fix as landing in the playbook, so the route stands); ⛔ not #15180 / #15184's dispositions; #17546 is the docs half of instance 1, separate. ## Instance count — a **third** occurrence of this class, from a different direction, recorded 2026-09-10T23:2xZ

This card names the method fault behind two false "dead key" verdicts. The same fault produced a third false figure today, on a different board and about a different kind of claim — which is what makes it a class rather than a spec-retirement problem.

| instance | the proxy | what a census showed |
|---|---|---|
| **#15180** (this card's instance 1) | 「read by nothing」 | read server-side, reaches the served document |
| **#15184** (instance 2) | 「a second, effectless spelling」 | alive in objectui's `ListView.tsx` |
| **#17379** | the card's own list of **7** packages | ~**36** areas, 114 files (triage measured) |
| ⭐ **objectui#8564** (new) | the marker `type Outcome` as a stand-in for "repaired" | the marker finds **2 of 11**; a per-file reading finds **6 of 9** repaired |

⭐ **objectui#8564's is the clearest specimen**, because the proxy and the census disagree on the *same tree at the same moment* — no staleness, no cross-repo rot, no timing. The marker is simply **a proxy for one repair lineage** and is structurally blind to the others. ⇒ It cannot be fixed by re-running it sooner.

⇒ That sharpens this card's remit: the fault is not only that **evidence rots**, it is that **a proxy is cheap and a census is not, and nothing in the loop asks which one a number came from.** A verdict carrying 「0 hits」 and a verdict carrying 「0 after enumerating the population」 are read identically today.

⚠️ objectui#8564 has been closed `not_planned` (its premise was falsified in both halves and the work had already landed). ⛔ It is recorded here as evidence for the class, ⛔ not as work.

⚠️ And the uncomfortable half, stated because it belongs on the record: **the false figure on objectui#8564 was triage's own**, written into the grading comment. The class is not something other seats do.
